title: Global report: one in nine migratory birds threatened with extinction
summary: A global report released September 11, 2026 found one in nine migratory bird species threatened with extinction, with 45% of all migratory species in decline. The slender-billed curlew was declared extinct in 2025, the first mainland Eurasian and African bird extinction in recent centuries.
takeaways: One in nine migratory bird species threatened with extinction; 45% of all migratory species in decline
Slender-billed curlew declared extinct in 2025—first global bird extinction in mainland Eurasia and Africa in recent centuries
Seven migratory bird species confirmed or suspected extinct over last 150 years
Threats: agricultural intensification, unsustainable hunting, pollution, invasive species, and global heating

title: mRNA lipid nanoparticles targeting tumor-associated macrophages for cancer immunotherapy
summary: Researchers developed mRNA lipid nanoparticles designed to target tumor-associated macrophages and enhance cytotoxic T lymphocyte-mediated cancer immunity.

title: 'Flamingo Revolution' in Albania Protests Kushner-Trump Resort and Government Corruption
summary: Thousands of Albanians are protesting in Tirana in the "Flamingo Revolution," the largest unrest since communism's collapse, initially sparked by a luxury mega-resort backed by Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump on a protected nature reserve. Protests have broadened into anti-corruption demonstrations a
takeaways: Largest protests in Albania since communism's collapse
Sparked by Kushner-Trump luxury resort on protected public nature reserve island
Escalated into broader anti-corruption challenge to PM Edi Rama's government
Protesters accuse administration of selling coastline to elites

title: JWST observes changing ring system around small body Chariklo
summary: James Webb Space Telescope detects variations in the rings of Chariklo, a small body 250 kilometers in diameter located at 17 times the Earth-Sun distance.

title: Indonesian wildfires threaten world's longest-running orangutan research site in Borneo
summary: Wildfires in Indonesia are threatening Cabang Panti research station in Gunung Palung national park, Borneo, home to one of the world's longest-running orangutan studies. Fires have burned within 200 metres of Rangkong research station; orangutans are fleeing the forests as an exceptionally strong E
takeaways: Research station: Cabang Panti, Gunung Palung national park, Borneo
Fires within 200 m of Rangkong satellite facility (~4 miles south of main camp)
Bornean orangutan population: hundreds at stations, 2,500+ in park; all three species critically endangered
Prof. Cheryl Knott (Boston University) led 32 years of research; orangutans fleeing
El Niño conditions: some West Kalimantan areas months without rainfall; fires escape annual control burns

title: Rare bird discovery in Ecuador catalyzes 30-year conservation model
summary: The discovery of a rare jocotoco antpitta in Ecuador's Andes in November 1997 catalyzed a foundation dedicated to biodiversity restoration that has become a globally recognized conservation model over 30 years.
takeaways: Jocotoco antpitta discovered November 1997 near Tapichalaca Lodge at 2,500 metres elevation
Bird unknown to science before discovery by ornithologist Robert Ridgely
Foundation established to restore cloud forest biodiversity in southern Ecuador
30-year conservation work became globally recognized model
Chestnut back, grey front, black crown, white face-patch; feeds on large earthworms

title: OMTX305 bispecific antibody shows T cell–mediated antitumor activity in solid tumor models
summary: The FAP × CD3 bispecific antibody OMTX305 demonstrated T cell-mediated antitumor effects in patient-derived ex vivo solid tumor models.

title: Bacterial import of glycol esters enables robust PET deconstruction
summary: Researchers demonstrated that engineered cellular systems can robustly transform PET deconstruction products by importing glycol esters.

title: Mutant p53 sensitizes KRAS lung cancer to immunotherapy by repressing SPP1
summary: Mutant p53 enhances responsiveness of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma to immunotherapy by suppressing SPP1 expression.

title: Acetyldigoxin targets LOXL4-driven matrix stiffening to restore CD8+ T cell function in lung cancer
summary: Acetyldigoxin reverses LOXL4-driven extracellular matrix stiffening to restore CD8+ T cell function and enhance tumor immunity in lung cancer.

title: Extreme California rainfall linked to climate teleconnection between Rocky Mountains and Tibetan Plateau
summary: Scientists identified a climate link between the Tibetan Plateau and Rocky Mountains where warm anomalies altered the jet stream, intensifying western U.S. weather.

title: Collagen-targeted protein MRI contrast agent enables early detection of lung cancer and metastasis
summary: A Science Advances study describes a collagen-targeted protein MRI contrast agent that can detect invasive lung cancer and multiorgan metastasis early.

title: Magnetically actuated nanoantennas show promise for wireless glioblastoma therapy
summary: A Science Advances study presents magnetically actuated nanoantennas as a potential wireless treatment approach for glioblastoma brain cancer.

title: TCR-JANUS engager proteins advance bispecific TCR-T cell cancer therapy
summary: Scientists develop TCR-JANUS engager proteins enabling bispecific targeting to overcome tumor heterogeneity in T cell immunotherapy.

title: Engineered suppressor tRNAs show promise for Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment
summary: Researchers develop engineered suppressor transfer RNAs as a potential therapeutic approach to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

title: Increased nitrogen loading in Gulf of Mexico undermines coral reef resilience
summary: Study reveals that elevated nitrogen loading from terrestrial sources into the Gulf of Mexico reduces the resilience of coral reef ecosystems.

title: Indigenous leaders in Bolivian Amazon warn carbon credit deals threaten land rights
summary: Community leaders in Pando region denounce opaque carbon credit agreements as government and companies rush to monetize the Amazon rainforest.

title: Rabbit populations booming in Australia due to rainfall and viral resistance
summary: Increased rainfall and growing resistance to viruses are driving a resurgence in Australia's rabbit populations, threatening native species.

title: Liquid metal-based stretchable electronics via programmable transfer printing
summary: Researchers developed a single-step programmable transfer printing method for creating spatial-variant stretchable electronics using liquid metal.

title: Transgenerational chromosome repair in bdelloid rotifers
summary: A study demonstrates that the asexual bdelloid rotifer Adineta vaga exhibits transgenerational chromosome repair mechanisms.

title: Laser-induced graphene system for real-time piezoresistive airflow sensing
summary: An integrated laser-induced graphene system decouples multiphysics interference to enable precise, real-time airflow sensing.

title: iCM exosome therapy with NIR-II imaging for myocardial ischemia treatment
summary: AT1R-mediated near-infrared imaging-guided induced cardiomyocyte exosome therapy showed promise for myocardial ischemia revascularization.

title: Victoria's Koala Population Halved and in Chronically Poor Health
summary: A delayed government report reveals Victoria's koala population is approximately half previous estimates and in poor health.

title: Tertiary lymphoid structure heterogeneity shapes immune niches and outcomes in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
summary: A Science Advances study reveals how tertiary lymphoid structure heterogeneity influences immune responses and clinical outcomes in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

title: Dysregulated m6A methylation drives premalignancy in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease
summary: A Science Advances paper identifies dysregulated m6A methylation via compensatory arginine methylation as a driver of premalignant progression in MASLD.

title: Traffic Noise Silences Gibbons' Dawn Chorus in Fragmented Forests
summary: Research suggests that increasing traffic noise from road development and habitat fragmentation is altering gibbons' characteristic early-morning vocalizations.

title: Benedict Cumberbatch on his documentary about planetary healing and resource extraction
summary: Actor Benedict Cumberbatch has gathered global experts for a documentary examining how to heal the planet amid what he calls 'the last grab of the extraction era.'
